raw.thesis: Narma is developing an "Enterprise Agentic Brain" for AI-first companies to address the challenges of deploying AI automation at scale. The core innovation lies in its three-layered architecture: an "Observe" layer with lightweight desktop sensors to capture work patterns, an "Intelligence Layer" that acts as a "Brain" to detect employee intent, business value of tasks, and "drift" in workflows, and an "Execution Layer" to automatically generate, deploy, and monitor AI agents for high-ROI opportunities. This system aims to provide "Continuous AI lift" by identifying where resources are being consumed inefficiently and where AI can intervene. It achieves this by focusing on a "Work Graph" and leveraging existing foundation models, rather than building new LLMs. The venture is positioned to replace existing manual processes or fragmented solutions for AI deployment and monitoring within AI-first enterprise environments. It helps enterprises pinpoint AI savings, measure ROI reliably, and manage workflow drift, which are common pain points for them. The founder's immediate goal appears to be building out this system to achieve continuous AI lift for enterprises. This venture is currently at the idea stage, with no observable signals of building or launching a product.
raw.product_description: Narma is an "Enterprise Agentic Brain" designed for AI-first companies to see, prove, and deploy AI automation at scale. It features a three-layered architecture: an "Observe" layer using lightweight desktop sensors to capture work patterns; an "Intelligence Layer" that acts as a "Brain" to detect employee intent, business value, and workflow drift; and an "Execution Layer" or "Agent Factory" that automatically generates, deploys, and monitors AI agents for high-ROI opportunities. This system leverages existing foundation models and focuses on a "Work Graph" to identify inefficiencies and areas where AI can assist mid-flow, ensuring "Continuous AI lift."
